RoomType.maps_to: driver.py's Event fight path (`_run_event`) always calls `_run_combat(event.pending_encounter, RoomType.MONSTER)`, matching MysteriousKnightEventEncounter.cs:9's `RoomType.Monster`. This unit is reached via TheLanternKey (events/the_lantern_key.py), a Combat-layout event (`is_combat_layout=True`): the encounter is generated at ROOM ENTRY (`generate_internal_combat_state` -> `_combat_layout.pregenerate_monster_hp`), mirroring `EventRoom.EnterInternal`/`GenerateInternalCombatState` (EventModel.cs:383-403) calling `GenerateMonstersWithSlots` before any option is chosen; the FIGHT option then reuses that generated state (`internal_combat_encounter`) rather than generating a second one, mirroring `EnterCombatWithoutExitingEvent`'s `ShouldCreateCombat = LayoutType != Combat` (EventModel.cs:624-628). Confirmed the encounter is constructed once per room-visit, not re-seeded on FIGHT.

AllPossibleMonsters.maps_to: no explicit sim field (whole-tree grep is empty, see battleworn_dummy_event); `MYSTERIOUS_KNIGHT_EVENT_ENCOUNTER.monster_classes = [MysteriousKnight]` already equals the C# superset `{MysteriousKnight}` (MysteriousKnightEventEncounter.cs:11) exactly.
AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: No sim representation of the concept, but a single-class non-branching roster IS its own superset here, so nothing is lost.

GenerateMonsters.maps_to: base `Encounter.create_monsters` (monsters/base.py), unmodified by MYSTERIOUS_KNIGHT_EVENT_ENCOUNTER (flail_knight.py:97-100). Roster: 1 MysteriousKnight, matching MysteriousKnightEventEncounter.cs:13-16's single-element list. Order/count: trivial (one element). Draw count: BOTH sides draw zero from any Rng in this method (no `base.Rng` call in the C# body). MysteriousKnight's own construction-time buffs -- StrengthPower 6 / PlatingPower 6 -- are applied directly in `MysteriousKnight.__init__` (flail_knight.py:89-94) via `PowerCmd.apply`, matching `MysteriousKnight.AfterAddedToRoom`'s `PowerCmd.Apply<StrengthPower>(...,6m,...)` / `PowerCmd.Apply<PlatingPower>(...,6m,...)` (MysteriousKnight.cs:13-14) exactly in amount. FlailKnight base stats (HP 101, FLAIL 9x2, RAM 15, WAR_CHANT +3 Str, opening move RAM, branch weights/repeat-caps) read against FlailKnight.cs:32-56 -- all non-ascension values and the RandomBranchState CannotRepeat/CanRepeatXTimes(max=2) shapes match; this is monster-tier territory but was read in full because MysteriousKnight IS this encounter's only monster.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.maps_to: EncounterModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false (EncounterModel.cs:39, inherited, not re-overridden). The sim never registers an Encounter as a hook listener anywhere (checked every `hooks.register(` call site in the repo).

guards.what: encounter/_entry_slug_mismatch: `MYSTERIOUS_KNIGHT_EVENT_ENCOUNTER.entry` = `MYSTERIOUS_KNIGHT_EVENT` (from `id="mysterious_knight_event"`), but the game's real `Id.Entry` for `MysteriousKnightEventEncounter` is `MYSTERIOUS_KNIGHT_EVENT_ENCOUNTER` (`StringHelper.Slugify(type.Name)` via `ModelDb.GetEntry`) -- the sim's id drops the '_ENCOUNTER' suffix. This is the encounter this batch confirmed is a Combat-layout event, so the wrong entry string is fed to `_combat_layout.pregenerate_monster_hp`'s `make_encounter_rng(seed, floor, encounter.entry)` call at ROOM ENTRY, not only at fight time. Executed: `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e9.py entry-slug-mismatch` prints MISMATCH.
guards.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). `Encounter` gained an explicit `entry_slug` field and `Encounter.entry` returns it when set, so this unit seeds `make_encounter_rng` with the game's real `ModelId.Entry` while keeping its sim id. A mechanical sweep of ALL 87 sim encounters against `src/Core/Models/Encounters/*.cs` (audit/tools/encounter_entry_sweep.py) found two more the unit batches had not checked — `fuzzy_wurm_crawler` (FuzzyWurmCrawlerWeak) and `overgrowth_crawlers_normal` (OvergrowthCrawlers) — and now reports MATCH for every one. Pinned by test/test_encounter_entry_slugs.py.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: Same mechanism as `battleworn_dummy_event/G1` and (LIVE) `punch_off_event/G1`. Dormant here because MysteriousKnightEventEncounter.GenerateMonsters (via the base `Encounter.create_monsters` this unit uses unmodified) draws zero values from the per-encounter Rng regardless of which entry string seeded it; `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e9.py dormant-4-zero-draws` confirms the sim's `create_monsters` output (class, slot_name, HP) is byte-identical under two unrelated seeds.
